headline: South Asia: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza.
- India: Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy.
- Persian Gulf Region: Drone attack on police base in Colombia injures three, including infant.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
- Military Times, 7 hours ago: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
Trump said he wanted to move forward with the controlled blasts but is putting the decision in the hands of the courts.
- Military Times, 11 hours ago: B-2 bomber wings awarded Presidential Unit Citation for Midnight Hammer.
The award marks the first time a bomber unit has been recognized with a President Unit Citation since the Vietnam War.
- Military Times, 8 hours ago: Under Hegseth, the OSS rides again — kind of.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth resurrected the OSS, created during the Second World War under "Wild Bill" Donovan.
- Military Times, 9 hours ago: VFW seeks veterans’ input on health care experiences in and out of VA.
Through early January, Veterans of Foreign Wars is conducting a survey of veterans on their health care experiences, including medical treatment received at the Department of Veterans Affairs or in private care.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Robbers reach end of road with rare armoured car heist convictions.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Robbers reach end of road with rare armoured car heist convictions.
A string of robberies targeting armoured money-courier companies has yielded two convictions in two months, but the attacks continue, with the latest incident occurring in Liguanea, St Andrew, earlier this month. The two recent convictions mark the first time in 17 years that individuals have faced sentencing following successful prosecutions for offences linked to armoured-car robberies since the last such conviction in 2009.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Generations bound by Howard.
WESTERN BUREAU: For generations, Howard University has been a home away from home for Jamaicans, where families have sent their children to acquire world-class skills, build successful careers and forge friendships that last a lifetime. From engineers and architects to doctors and lawyers, the historically Black institution in Washington, DC, has helped shape the professional journeys of Jamaicans, with some families establishing traditions that span generations.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russians launch airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia: six injured – photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: Russians launch airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia: six injured – photos.
Six people have been injured in Russian strikes on the city of Zaporizhzhia.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 12 hours ago: Germany's Merz urges Russia to stop "dangerous provocations" after missiles fall in Poland.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged Russia to stop dangerous provocations after Russian missiles fell in Poland, pledging full solidarity with Warsaw.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: "A little miracle": three cats rescued at site of Russian strike in Dymer, one found completely buried – photo.
Rescue workers found a cat under the rubble of a building destroyed in a Russian attack in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast. The animal was completely buried under sand, dust and construction debris but survived. The cat was named Dym and taken to a veterinary clinic.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: NATO strengthens protection after Russian missiles violate Polish airspace.
Poland's Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz says allied aircraft will complement ground-based systems, Polish F-16s and other NATO fighter jets.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Back to 1936? Civil war ghosts haunt Spanish election campaign.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Back to 1936? Civil war ghosts haunt Spanish election campaign.
With the far right poised to enter government, politicians are reopening the wounds of a war that began 90 years ago.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Peace in Ukraine won’t end Russian sabotage in Europe, Poland warns.
Poland’s intelligence minister says Moscow's hybrid campaign against Europe could persist whether the war goes Russia’s way or not.
- Balkan Insight, 12 hours ago: Serbia’s Student Movement Criticises European Parliament’s Vukovar Resolution.
Student movement says draft resolution marking 35th anniversary of Croatian town's fall offers only 'one-sided interpretation of the past' and ignores Serb suffering elsewhere during the Croatia war.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Drone attack on police base in Colombia injures three, including infant.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Drone attack on police base in Colombia injures three, including infant.
Far-right President De la Espriella steps up offensive as rebel groups strike back with drone strikes, roadside bombs.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Defense Ministry treating 92,300 wounded veterans, up 31,500 since start of war.
A total of 62% of the 31,500 who have been wounded since the start of the Israel-Hamas War have been dealing with mental health injuries, the ministry’s data showed.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Philippine Embassy in Israel holds ceremony memorializing Filipino victims of war, terror.
"We will not forget the Filipinos and Israelis murdered together by Palestinian terrorists and the Iranian terror regime," Israel's Foreign Ministry wrote.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Qatar PM looks to revive US-Iran talks after meeting Rubio.
Qatar’s Prime Minister says he’s working towards deescalating tensions between Iran and the US.
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 18 hours ago: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The United Nations and the United States have condemned Sunday's drone attacks in Sudan's capital, Khartoum, which damaged a civilian neighborhood and UN premises, as Sudan renewed allegations that drones used in attacks across its territory were launched from Ethiopia.
- Africanews, 15 hours ago: Libyan naval forces remain on high alert after strike on Russian vessel in Benghazi.
A military official says that naval forces in eastern Libya will remain on high alert to counter any threat after attacks targeted two vessels, including at least one Russian ship, off Benghazi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that Ukrainian forces were behind the strikes.
- Africanews, 22 hours ago: Drone strikes hit homes and UN premises in Sudan's capital.
The United Nations confirmed that one of its premises, with UN personnel inside, was damaged in the attacks. It condemned the risks posed to humanitarian workers in civilian areas.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: UN calls for probe after drone attacks hit ships off Libya.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for either strike on Sunday off the port city of Benghazi, but they came as Ukrainian forces stepped up attacks against Russia far from the front lines.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Is South Africa Losing Ground Against HIV? These Four Graphs Offer a Warning.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 19 hours ago: South Africa: Is South Africa Losing Ground Against HIV? These Four Graphs Offer a Warning.
[Bhekisisa] Findings from one of the world's largest ongoing population surveys tracking HIV, in rural KwaZulu-Natal, are "a sobering warning", researchers say. All four indicators they analysed show that the momentum in bringing the HIV epidemic under control has been lost -- which could mean it could start growing again. It's a pivotal moment, experts say. South Africa will have to get smart about testing people and getting them on to treatment or prevention if the country were to end HIV as a public health

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza.
CAIRO/JERUSALEM: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three people in Gaza on Monday, including a man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency UNRWA, the relief age­ncy and local health officials said. The UNRWA worker, whom medics named as Adel Al-Helo, was working near a well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the enclave’s north, the agency and medics said. Three others were wounded in the strike, they said. “The initial reports indicate that the strike hit a target on the street near the water well, which was manned by UNRWA staff and a guard.
- The Hindu - International, 11 hours ago: 17 killed in Saudi attack on Yemeni city: Houthis.
Coalition airstrikes on telecoms facilities killed 17 workers, wounded 11 more, and caused the “total destruction” of administrative buildings, staff housing, a mosque and other sites, the Houthis’ Telecommunications Ministry said
- The Hindu - International, 11 hours ago: Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran.
War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Pakistan has Portugal's 'full support' for GSP+ status, visiting FM says during talks in Islamabad.
Pakistan has Portugal’s “full support” for the European Union’s (EU) GSP+ status, Portuguese Minister of State and Foreign Affairs Paulo Rangel said on Monday during delegation-level talks between the two countries held in Islamabad. The Portuguese minister arrived in the capital on Sunday on a two-day visit. Pakistan’s current GSP+ status is set to expire in 2027, after which Islamabad will seek a renewal.
India - bottom line: Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy.
- Times of India - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, AllAfrica - Conflict, Ukrainska Pravda, The Moscow Times, one hour ago: Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy.
Russia's military conducted attacks on military sites in Ukraine's Sumy region using drones and missile strikes. In a separate incident, an overnight attack in Zaporizhzhia resulted in injuries to 11 individuals, including severe cases. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued warnings about impending Russian strike preparations while urging increased military aid from allies. He emphasized the importance of anti-ballistic missile systems for Ukraine's defense against aggression.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Pune techie beats girlfriend to death, sits besides body entire night.
In Hinjewadi, Pune, a software engineer was arrested after allegedly killing his girlfriend during an argument. The couple had been in a relationship for three-and-a-half years and often fought over trivial issues. Following a dinner outing, a violent argument escalated, leading to the woman's death. Her cousin reported her unresponsiveness to the police, prompting their intervention. The police discovered her unconscious, and she was pronounced dead shortly after.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: US probes Iran, Russia link after 50 vessels face cyberattack: Report.
Washington is investigating Iran's potential involvement in numerous cyberattacks against energy tankers carrying hazardous materials. This probe includes incidents where vessels received bomb threats alleging possible explosions. The investigation comes amid concerns that the conflict may expand beyond the Middle East into cyber operations. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported three tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: ‘Severe explosions, fires’: Iran claims 3 oil tankers struck mines in Hormuz.
Three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours. Iranian military officials claimed these vessels were escorted by the US Navy while navigating the passage. According to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, US military support could not prevent these incidents from occurring. The IRGC warned vessel owners against ignoring maritime warnings and unauthorized routes through the region.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Ukraine attacks Russian freighter accused of smuggling North Korean arms in past.
- NK News, one hour ago: Ukraine attacks Russian freighter accused of smuggling North Korean arms in past.
The Ukrainian military carried out a drone strike on a Russian cargo vessel that has been suspected of smuggling North Korean weapons in the past, in an operation that also destroyed a Russian warship off Libya’s coast, according to Kyiv on Monday. The attack on Sunday struck the cargo freighter Angara and sank the Russian […]
- NK News, 20 hours ago: US senator warns North Korea growing ‘more lethal’ due to Ukraine war.
North Korea’s deployment of troops to support Russia’s war against Ukraine is turning the country into a more capable military threat, a prominent U.S. senator has warned, arguing that this will constrain Washington’s freedom to act. Speaking at the Halifax International Security Forum over the weekend, Democratic Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware said cooperation among […]

SEOUL, Nov. 24 (Yonhap) -- Several Russian warplanes briefly entered South Korea...
- Yonhap News Agency, 2 hours ago: Samsung promotes 131 executives, rewards semiconductor talent in reshuffle.
SEOUL, Nov. 24 (Yonhap) -- Samsung Electronics Co. on Tuesday announced its annu...
Asia - bottom line: Israel leadership rivals clash over Iran threat ahead of coalition talks.
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Israel leadership rivals clash over Iran threat ahead of coalition talks.
Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, said he saw no immediate reason for attacking Iran on Monday, contradicting caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who warned against playing down “grave threats”. The remarks from both politicians came hours before their parties were due to meet for the third time to discuss possible coalition-building, after lengthy negotiations the day before delivered no breakthrough. Eisenkot has until December 6 – a deadline which...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: Philippines touts power cable to Malaysia’s Sabah, yet Sabah is in no rush.
A proposed undersea power link between Malaysia’s Sabah state and the southern Philippines has been hailed by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr as a major step towards Asean’s vision for a regional electricity grid, yet questions remain over whether it can deliver cheaper, more reliable power. Announcing the proposed Sabah–Mindanao connection on November 17, Marcos said the bloc had made “some serious progress” towards cross-border electricity trading, with plans now extending beyond...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Hacked Russian data suggests nearly 500,000 soldiers dead, reports say.
Data allegedly stolen by hackers from Russia’s statistics agency Rosstat show the number of recorded Russian military dead is approaching 500,000, several Russian media outlets and German news magazine Der Spiegel reported on Monday. The outlets said they had gained access to the data set, which the hacker groups Cyberpartisans and Silent Crow are said to have taken in an attack on the agency. Reports say the groups are close to the Belarusian opposition or to pro-Ukrainian collectives. Rosstat...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Malaysia’s Anwar says Beijing ‘extremely reasonable’ in South China Sea talks.
China has been “extremely reasonable” in its negotiations with Malaysia over their competing claims in the South China Sea and discussions will continue as long as certain core sensitivities are respected, according to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. He said each country had “red lines” it would not compromise on: areas China considered too close to its interests, and waters Malaysia considered “undisputedly Malaysian borders”. “OK, we don’t touch that,” he said in an interview with the South...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Israel's bombardment has turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland'.
- ABC News Australia, 6 hours ago: Israel's bombardment has turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland'.
New research suggests more than 99 per cent of the Gaza Strip shows signs of contamination from Israeli attacks.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Luxury resort caretakers hope for less intense cyclone season.
Couple who survived 'apocalyptic' Cyclone Fina in underground bunker brace for another remote caretaker stint
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Australian social media figure enlists to fight in Ukraine war against Russia.
A prominent social media commentator from the Northern Territory has become a soldier fighting in the Ukrainian war against Russia. Shannon Joyce says during his time with Ukraine's armed forces he's had some "close calls".
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Prisoner who drank toilet water not deemed high risk before death in custody.
A prisoner who cut himself and exhibited concerning behaviour in the days before he killed himself in a Western Australian jail was not deemed to be at high risk of self-harm, a coronial inquest hears.
